question: Is there Takeda-specific evidence supporting PHVS as a strategic acquisition candidate?
conclusion: Credible strategic fit and historical lineage; no current bid, discussions, stake or sale process identified in a bounded public-source pass. No acquisition probability assigned.

observed.fact: Modig was CFO at Jerini through its 2008 sale to Shire. Jerini developed icatibant/Firazyr, a B2 antagonist. Takeda acquired Shire in 2019.
observed.interpretation: Same target and asset lineage; does not establish current personal relationships or negotiations.

observed.fact: FY2025 ended March 31, 2026: Takhzyro global JPY223.9bn; US140.7bn; Japan3.4bn; Europe/Canada58.7bn; growth/emerging21.1bn.
observed.locator: Product geographic revenue table, printed page 49 / PDF page 50

observed.fact: Takhzyro US revenue fell 6.4% in reported JPY; worldwide rose 0.3%. FY2026 guidance JPY239bn, +7% reported but 0% constant currency.
observed.caution: Reported geographic changes include FX; not patient losses or evidence oral competition caused decline.

observed.fact: Firazyr FY2025 global revenue JPY16.0bn versus18.0bn prior year, -11.2% reported; US9.1bn.
observed.interpretation: IR could rebuild a smaller shrinking rescue business; XR has larger existing franchise overlap.

observed.fact: Adjusted net debt/EBITDA 2.6x versus capital allocation target 2x.
observed.interpretation: Capital allocation constraint, not proof inability to transact.

observed.fact: Takeda BD statement January11,2025 highlights Shire acquisition, Nimbus oral TYK2 acquisition and licensing transactions; criteria include strategic fit and investment returns.
observed.interpretation: Acquisition and licensing are both available structures; no HAE-specific acquisition mandate.

inferences: Takeda could use existing HAE specialist relationships, access infrastructure and international organization; magnitude of synergy unmeasured.
Ex-US execution discount in standalone PHVS model should be reconsidered in a separate Takeda ownership scenario, not erased in standalone case.
IR complements Takhzyro at a portfolio level; efficacy and safety of a particular combination still require evidence. Same-B2 lineage applies to Firazyr, not Takhzyro.

Buying PHVS could retain patients who otherwise migrate to competitor orals. Must compare combined portfolio under ownership with realistic no-deal erosion; cannot assume all PHVS sales incremental while Takhzyro stays unchanged.
counterarguments: Purchase price and competing capital needs may outweigh synergies.
Cannibalization of Takhzyro; potential competition review needs specialist assessment, not an assumed prohibition.
Regional licensing could achieve strategic goals without buying PHVS.
Clinical and commercial superiority is not established by cross-trial headlines.
model_treatment: No standalone model change. Buyer scenario should explicitly vary ex-US execution, acquisition costs, SG&A reuse and net portfolio cannibalization; do not mechanically apply current Takhzyro geographic ratio to PHVS.
limitation: Public strategic fit cannot identify confidential discussions. No deal rumor treated as evidence; no probability or premium calibrated. Bounded primary-source search and existing local financial data reused.
